SQLAlchemy echo logging records SQL and bound values. Normal writes expose email addresses, bcrypt hashes, invite codes, note contents, and profile data to process logs.

extra.message: An attacker-controlled preferences cookie is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads() before every request. A malicious pickle yields unauthenticated arbitrary code execution.

A profile-image URL controlled by an authenticated user reaches urlopen() with no scheme, host, or address restriction. Responses from internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and file:// URLs are read and stored for retrieval.
urlopen() has no timeout and response.read() has no byte limit. A slow or unbounded attacker-controlled endpoint can occupy workers indefinitely or exhaust server memory.

User-supplied note text is stored without server-side sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. A public note therefore executes attacker HTML or JavaScript for every authenticated user loading the home page.

extra.message: The preferences cookie is set without HttpOnly here and again in after_request. Stored XSS can replace it with a malicious pickle, which the pre-request hook then deserializes into server-side code execution.
Nginx listens only on HTTP port 80 and defines no TLS listener or HTTPS redirect. Login passwords, session cookies, notes, and account data are exposed to network interception and modification.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: POST /account/image uses ambient session authentication and changes persistent profile data, but neither the form nor handler validates a CSRF token. A cross-site request can change a victim's image and trigger the server-side URL fetch.

POST /account accepts cookie-authenticated email, password, and is_admin changes without CSRF validation. A forged request can change a victim's password or privileges without knowing the current password.

POST /notes creates a note under the cookie-authenticated user's identity without validating a CSRF token. A forged request can insert persistent, public attacker content, including the stored-XSS payload accepted by the renderer.
POST /notes/<note_id>/delete performs a cookie-authenticated deletion without CSRF validation. A cross-site form can force deletion of a predictable note ID.

The admin-only registration-code creation operation relies on the session cookie but validates no CSRF token. A cross-site request from an authenticated administrator's browser can create persistent invite credentials.

POST /login accepts cross-site form submissions without a CSRF token. An attacker can submit their own valid credentials and force a victim's browser into the attacker's account, causing subsequent victim data to be stored there.
Logout is a state-changing GET request protected only by an ambient session cookie. A cross-site navigation or embedded resource can log a victim out without consent.
Registration requires only a nonempty password and applies no minimum length or strength requirement. The account-update form likewise permits replacement with trivial credentials.

POST /account lacks login_required and performs a fresh bcrypt hash before session.merge() rejects an anonymous user. Repeated unauthenticated requests with differing password fields can cheaply pin CPU and exhaust workers.
The short-circuit condition runs expensive bcrypt verification only when the email exists. Repeated timing measurements can distinguish registered email addresses despite the generic error message.
After a valid invite is supplied, existing emails receive a distinct 'User already exists' response while new emails create an account. This response discrepancy discloses account existence.
A password change is committed without revoking or versioning existing Flask-Login sessions. A previously stolen session cookie remains authenticated after the account owner changes the password.

The CSV exporter copies attacker-controlled table text and only escapes quotes. Cells beginning with =, +, -, or @ remain spreadsheet formulas and can execute external-data or command-capable formulas when the export is opened.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The home-page query materializes every owned or public note with .all(), while note creation has no quota or pagination. An authenticated attacker can flood public notes so every user's home request allocates and renders the entire collection.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
